A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CyberGym-E2E research. All 15 pages in each version, including tables, figures and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original agent evaluations on 615-task and 920-task benchmarks (Tables 3–4), plus budget, feedback, memorization and trajectory analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds qualitative observations about alternative and shallow patches in Section 4.2.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction pipeline, agent workflows and execution-based validation remain unchanged. The additional LLM judge mentioned in v2 is a suggested complement, not an implemented component.

E1.justification: Both versions already include the initial 615 tasks and expanded 920 vulnerabilities across 139 projects, with patch-only and end-to-end evaluation. Appendix Table 9 is identical.

E2.justification: Tables 3–5 retain the same model–harness combinations and comparisons involving Claude Code, OpenHands, Codex and Gemini CLI. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The S1–S4 validation stages, $10/90-minute main evaluation budgets, uncapped Opus evaluations and feedback protocols are retained. The shallow-patch discussion clarifies existing scoring rather than changing it.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 adds a brief qualitative patch-quality analysis distinguishing alternative root-cause fixes from shallow crash-site guards. Existing budget, feedback, memorization and trajectory analyses are unchanged; no new quantified ablation is reported.

E5.justification: Table 8 retains the same Fisher exact tests, Z-tests and p-values. Neither version introduces different repeated-run, seed or uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: All tabulated numerical results remain unchanged. Section 4.2 newly reports that many successful patches fix the same root cause at different locations and that a small fraction of patches are shallow; these qualitative findings are unquantified.

T1.justification: No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations or formal evaluation properties are revised. Neither version presents theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same benchmark, scalability and end-to-end evaluation contributions. The central finding that vulnerability discovery constrains overall success is unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 explains why patch similarity can reject legitimate alternative fixes and explicitly acknowledges that shallow fixes can receive success credit. It recommends further review of generated patches and suggests supplementary LLM judging, qualifying the practical meaning of benchmark success.

D1.justification: Build and validation details, evaluation budgets, appendix prompts and dataset access information are retained. Appendices A–B contain no implementation or reproducibility changes.

R1.justification: The cited literature, benchmark comparison in Table 1 and substantive positioning against prior work remain unchanged. No references are added or removed.

P1.justification: v2 adds the patch-quality paragraph and makes localized wording, terminology and punctuation edits, including changing PoC development to PoC generation. The section organization and appendices remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 2 moves from the upper-right to the lower-left of page 4, several tables have tighter spacing, and surrounding text reflows. All figures and tables retain their displayed content.

improvement.justification: The new Section 4.2 discussion improves transparency by acknowledging that passing validation does not guarantee a root-cause repair and by recommending further review. This addresses an interpretive gap in v1, but the observations remain unquantified and the validation limitation itself is unresolved, so the overall gain is limited.
